answer: Each Ember agent boots inside a TEE that, during a remote attestation handshake, signs a unique enclave measurement tied to a hardware‑bound key and publishes the hash into the canyon‑indexed ledger. Validators cross‑reference the hash against a grove of registered keys, enforce a one‑per‑node rule, and only accept a voyage request from an enclave whose measurement has not been seen before. An attacker must purchase a separate TEE‑enabled host for every fake identity, incurring a minimum cost of $2,500 per identity plus a 48‑hour lock‑up of the host’s collateral.
